chunks: We have indeed warned you of a calamity near at hand, a day when man will see what he had sent (of his deeds) ahead, and the unbeliever will say: 'Woe alas. Ah would that I were dust!'

key_terms.يَا لَيْتَنِي: O that I were / Ah would that I were

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about the Day of Judgment and the disbeliever's regret?
ai.summary: In Surah Al-Mursalat, this verse underscores the immediacy of the Hour, where the weight of one's own deeds becomes the primary witness against the individual. Shia exegesis often highlights the psychological torment of the disbeliever wishing to return to dust, reflecting the regret of those who failed to prepare for the Hereafter through faith and righteous action. This moment serves as a stark reminder of personal accountability, where deeds are not merely recorded but actively confront their doer.
